title: Classical Mathematics Lean 4 Formalization Candidates
description:
Small Lean 4 / Mathlib-style package of useful formal mathematics candidates inspired by the historical mathematics transcription project and related side work. The package contains Lean sources, build logs, copied Lean/Lake/Mathlib toolchain metadata, planning notes, and provenance for one failed/superseded batch.

Green candidate modules. The current green classical modules include a Camille Jordan affine-line group order example over ZMod p, a Jordan primitive-root count modulo a prime, an Ernst Steinitz perfect-field/Frobenius-surjectivity criterion, and a Heinrich Weber modular-function cubic represented as a real polynomial identity. The package also includes a split-zero sidecar formalization connected to the separate split-support/projectification side paper.

Public framing. This is useful Lean/mathlib-style library-candidate material: small formalized statements, examples, identities, and reusable developments that may be useful additions to Lean because Lean benefits from more formalized mathematics. It is not a proof, archive-audit, or certification layer for the transcription/translation corpus; it is not source-fidelity evidence for scanned editions and not a critical-edition claim. Older local names such as ClassicalAudit are legacy namespace/worktree labels only.

Corrections, Lean build improvements, theorem-map additions, and packaging fixes can be suggested through GitHub issues or pull requests: https://github.com/KokunoYumeto/modern-latex-manuscripts.
